ENG_064.context: A point without a measurement number was noticed in the as-built drawing.
ENG_064.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will personally arrange for the link between the point and its measurement to be restored and record it in the as-built drawing.
options.B: I will point out to the drafter that the point cannot be confirmed without tracing the measurement.
options.C: I will find the source file and assign the number according to the procedure.
options.D: I will report the omission, check the source file and complete the drawing.

ENG_065.context: The supervisor asks to transfer an axis to the neighbouring area because access is blocked.
ENG_065.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will explain the conditions under which an auxiliary point keeps its accuracy.
options.B: I will help the crew clear a safe spot for the control point.
options.C: I will set out the control scheme and choose an accessible spot together.
options.D: I will propose a spot for an offset point and agree access for checking it together with the supervisor.

ENG_066.context: Before the night shift, the established points need to be handed over to the next survey crew.
ENG_066.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will do a joint walk-round and show the marking of the points.
options.B: I will update the log and check the key points together with the new crew.
options.C: I will agree a joint check of the points with the night shift and record the handover result in the log.
options.D: I will record the coordinates, elevations and control method in the log.

ENG_067.context: After heavy rain, a control benchmark on a temporary structure may have shifted.
ENG_067.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the benchmark against the base and record the check results before use.
options.B: I will check the benchmark against the stable network and register the confirmed status of the point.
options.C: I will close the survey onto stable control points and compare the elevations.
options.D: I will take the benchmark out of use until a documented check is done.

ENG_068.context: Setting-out coordinates from different contractors give different positions for the same joint.
ENG_068.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the contractors' source systems and personally propose a procedure for resolving the coordinate conflict.
options.B: I will compare the coordinate systems, the source axes and the file versions.
options.C: I will point out to both sides the exact discrepancy and the need for a single basis.
options.D: I will check the transformations and present the confirmed discrepancy.

ENG_069.context: On site, people often forget to mark the date on control marks.
ENG_069.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check which marks are actually used and how they are updated.
options.B: I will agree on marking with the supervisors and help update the current marks.
options.C: I will find out the reasons and introduce clear dated marking together.
options.D: I will collect cases of missing dates together with the workers and check where it is most convenient to confirm that marks are current.

ENG_070.context: The contractor demands the as-built drawing while the control traverse has not yet been processed.
ENG_070.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will finish processing the traverse and formalise the control results.
options.B: I will explain the timing and issue the drawing after checking the misclosure and formalising it.
options.C: I will personally arrange for the traverse processing to be completed and establish the procedure for issuing the confirmed drawing.
options.D: I will report that the accuracy of the drawing has not yet been confirmed.

ENG_071.context: During a floor handover, the neighbouring crew cannot find the established axis marks.
ENG_071.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the log and restore the reference with a control measurement together with the crew.
options.B: I will suggest searching together with the crew using the diagram and take responsibility for confirming the axes we find.
options.C: I will show the coordinates and condition of the valid points from the log.
options.D: I will organise a joint search with the supervisor and mark the axes found.

ENG_072.context: The concrete batch certificate shows a class that does not match the site's order.
ENG_072.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the certificate with the order and file a request to confirm the properties of the actual batch.
options.B: I will check the certificate, the order and the truck mixer's marking.
options.C: I will suspend acceptance of the batch and record the non-conformity.
options.D: I will check the documents and register the deviation until those responsible decide.

ENG_073.context: The strength of the control specimens is close to the threshold, and the report shows unusual scatter.
ENG_073.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the conditions of sampling, storage and testing, and the calculation.
options.B: I will tell the quality engineer that I doubt the reliability of the results and request a check.
options.C: I will check the testing chain and propose a repeat analysis with justification.
options.D: I will check the reasons for the scatter and personally propose to the head of the laboratory a procedure for a repeat analysis.

ENG_074.context: The same kind of remark about the concrete surface recurs on several pour sections.
ENG_074.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will discuss with the site what data is needed to prevent the defect.
options.B: I will analyse the recurrence and help the site check the cause on the spot.
options.C: I will collect data on the conditions in which the defects appeared together with the site teams and test a hypothesis common to the pour sections.
options.D: I will compare the locations, shifts and placement conditions to find a pattern.

ENG_075.context: The contractor asks you to mark the incoming inspection of rebar as done before the certificates arrive.
ENG_075.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will clearly explain the restriction and record the actual stage of the inspection.
options.B: I will request the set of rebar confirmations myself and record the incoming inspection status until they are checked.
options.C: I will explain that without confirmed documents the acceptance status is not complete.
options.D: I will carry out the check that is possible and note in the log that the documents are awaited.

ENG_076.context: The supervisor considers a mandatory control point in the quality plan unnecessary because of deadlines.
ENG_076.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will suggest discussing the arrangements for the control point with the supervisor and take responsibility for explaining its role.
options.B: I will state the basis for the control point and the consequences of skipping it.
options.C: I will propose jointly planning the time for the check in the site schedule.
options.D: I will explain the requirement and help agree the check without disrupting the work.

ENG_077.context: During sampling, the new shift did not receive a record of where the previous samples were taken.
ENG_077.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the logs, the specimen markings and the work section diagram.
options.B: I will contact both shifts and help clarify the location from the confirmations.
options.C: I will check the records and, together with the shifts, document a reliable link to the sampling location.
options.D: I will agree the sampling location with the previous shift and record the restored traceability of the sample.

ENG_078.context: The calibration of the compaction test instrument has expired.
ENG_078.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will take the instrument out of service and record the need for metrological verification.
options.B: I will check the status and arrange a replacement with an instrument that has valid calibration.
options.C: I will check the instrument's status with the metrologist and formalise the use of a confirmed replacement.
options.D: I will check the certificate, the instrument ID and the available spare instrument.

ENG_079.context: The weld inspection results differ between two methods.
ENG_079.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the reports and propose a confirmed plan for an additional check.
options.B: I will compare the conditions of the two inspection methods and present the grounds for an additional check myself.
options.C: I will check the scope of applicability of the methods and the inspection conditions.
options.D: I will tell those responsible that the conclusion requires a technical reconciliation.

ENG_080.context: Remarks about joint sealing recur at the same detail.
ENG_080.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will collect information on the sealing conditions together with the workers and check the common causes of the recurring remark.
options.B: I will group the defects by conditions, materials and workers.
options.C: I will discuss with the supervisors checking the substrate preparation before sealing.
options.D: I will find the recurring factor and clarify the control step together with the site.

ENG_081.context: The log shows an air temperature that nobody measured on site.
ENG_081.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will point out that an unconfirmed value cannot be passed off as a measured one.
options.B: I will take an actual measurement and record the time and the instrument.
options.C: I will explain the reason for the correction and formalise a confirmed measurement.
options.D: I will personally arrange for the source of the temperature to be clarified and record the confirmed information in the log.

ENG_082.context: The crew asks to be told in advance the acceptance criteria for the substrate before finishing.
ENG_082.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will do a short walk-round of typical inspection points with the foreman.
options.B: I will explain the criteria and demonstrate how to check them together on site.
options.C: I will suggest reviewing the substrate acceptance criteria together with the crew and take responsibility for explaining the disputed points.
options.D: I will name the parameters to be checked and where the tolerances are set.

ENG_083.context: Materials from different batches but with a common label were found in the warehouse.
ENG_083.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check traceability and re-label the batches together with the warehouse.
options.B: I will agree with the warehouse on separating the batches and establish traceable labelling when materials are issued.
options.C: I will check the labelling and documents of each batch, then separate the records.
options.D: I will help the warehouse set up separate zones and clear labels.

ENG_084.context: The laboratory test report has no reference to the measurement method.
ENG_084.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the test records with the method used and formalise a clarification of the report before it is passed on.
options.B: I will check the source logs and the method used.
options.C: I will return the report for completion according to the quality procedure.
options.D: I will check the method against the log and formalise a correction to the report.

ENG_085.context: A geometry check of a finished opening shows a value at the edge of the tolerance.
ENG_085.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the tool, the measurement method and the tolerance according to the current documentation.
options.B: I will tell the supervisor about the borderline result and propose a control measurement.
options.C: I will repeat the measurement and present the confirmed value relative to the tolerance.
options.D: I will check the borderline measurement together with the inspector and personally explain the basis for the decision to the site.

ENG_086.context: Non-conformity cards often do not state which drawing was used.
ENG_086.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will help the inspectors add a revision field to the working card.
options.B: I will check the reasons for the omissions and agree a mandatory revision check.
options.C: I will collect examples of omissions together with the authors of the cards and check where the drawing reference gets lost.
options.D: I will trace at what stage the revision number gets lost.

ENG_087.context: After a soil test, the supervisor asks to be told the result before the measurements have been processed.
ENG_087.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will tell him when it will be issued and hand over the confirmed report after the calculation.
options.B: I will personally arrange for processing of the measurements to be completed and establish the procedure for issuing the confirmed result.
options.C: I will explain that preliminary readings are not yet a conclusion.
options.D: I will process the data and formalise the report in the established way.

ENG_088.context: The contractor offers its material as an equivalent to the specified material without agreed properties.
ENG_088.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will suggest clarifying the substitute's parameters together with the contractor and take responsibility for discussing the assessment conditions.
options.B: I will set out the list of properties and the need to approve the substitution.
options.C: I will help collect the data sheets and organise a review by specialists.
options.D: I will explain the criteria and help send the package for approval.

ENG_089.context: Before concrete works, some of the inspection checklists are filled in by different shifts.
ENG_089.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the mandatory fields and examples of correct completion.
options.B: I will hold a short review with both shifts and answer questions.
options.C: I will clarify a single template and check the first entries together with the shifts.
options.D: I will agree with the shifts on how to fill in the checklists and establish checks on the handover of open items.

ENG_090.context: During sampling of crushed stone, the bag marking did not match the batch number on the delivery note.
ENG_090.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will isolate the sample until its origin is established and note the discrepancy.
options.B: I will check traceability and resolve the non-conformity in writing before testing.
options.C: I will compare the sample marking with the primary records and formalise a confirmed identification.
options.D: I will check the seal, the sampling location and the source documents.

ENG_091.context: A moisture content check gave a result noticeably different from the previous shift.
ENG_091.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will repeat the check and explain to the site the reasons or the limit of uncertainty.
options.B: I will check the conditions of the new measurement and present the shift with an explanation of the difference from the previous result myself.
options.C: I will check the method, the condition of the sample and the records of the sampling conditions.
options.D: I will inform the site of the confirmed deviation and the need for a check.

ENG_092.context: On one section the inspector is regularly called late before concealed work is closed up.
ENG_092.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will collect the reasons for late calls together with the site team and check at what stage the readiness signal gets lost.
options.B: I will check the intervals between requests and actual closing up.
options.C: I will agree a convenient call window and early notification with the supervisors.
options.D: I will analyse the causes of the delays and help introduce a notification schedule.

ENG_093.context: The inspection report states a defect category that has not been confirmed by measurement.
ENG_093.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will say that the category cannot be confirmed without the required measurement.
options.B: I will return the report for an additional check and record a remark.
options.C: I will explain the shortcoming, carry out the check and update the report based on the result.
options.D: I will personally arrange confirmation of the defect category and record the basis in the inspection report.

ENG_094.context: A new laboratory shift is unsure how to take samples from a non-uniform batch.
ENG_094.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will hold a joint review of the batch and help prepare a sampling plan.
options.B: I will explain the method and check the sampling locations together with the shift.
options.C: I will suggest going through the sampling plan together with the shift and take responsibility for explaining the chosen approach.
options.D: I will explain the requirements for the sampling scheme and the limits of an acceptable decision.

ENG_095.context: At handover of the building to the client, several minor remarks on material labelling remain open.
ENG_095.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check each remark and confirm the corrections together with the teams.
options.B: I will agree a labelling check with those responsible and record the verified closure of each entry.
options.C: I will check the register of remarks against the actual labels and documents.
options.D: I will help the warehouse and the site distribute the corrections by location.
